Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He gave me many advices."

Sentence Correction.subject: English

Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "The scenery of Swat are breathtaking."

Sentence Correction.subject: English

Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He is senior than me in service."

options.D: He is more senior than me in service.

options.D: Mathematics have been a difficult subject.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He died from malaria."
Sentence Correction.explanation: One dies "of" a disease, not "from" or "by".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "Unless you do not work hard, you will fail."

options.A: Unless you work hard, you will fail.
options.B: Unless you did not work hard, you will fail.
options.C: Unless you will work hard, you will fail.
options.D: Unless you do work hard, you will not fail.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Unless" already contains the negative meaning; adding "do not" is a double negative.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He asked me that what my name was."

options.A: He asked me what my name was.
options.B: He asked me that what was my name.
options.C: He asked me what was my name.
options.D: He asked that my name what was.

Sentence Correction.explanation: In indirect WH-questions, conjunction "that" must be omitted.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "Between you and I, this secret must be kept."

options.A: Between you and me, this secret must be kept.
options.B: Between you and myself, this secret must be kept.
options.C: Between he and I, this secret must be kept.
options.D: Between you and mine, this secret must be kept.

Sentence Correction.explanation: Prepositions require objective case pronouns ("Between you and me").

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He ordered for a cup of tea."

options.A: He ordered a cup of tea.
options.B: He ordered with a cup of tea.
options.C: He ordered to a cup of tea.
options.D: He ordered about a cup of tea.

Sentence Correction.explanation: As a transitive verb, "ordered" directly takes its object without "for".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "She resembles to her mother."
Sentence Correction.explanation: "Resemble" is a transitive verb and takes no preposition.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He entered into the room quietly."

options.B: He entered inside the room quietly.
options.C: He entered to the room quietly.
options.D: He entered within the room quietly.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Enter" meaning physical entry takes no preposition ("entered the room").

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "I, you and he committed a blunder."

options.A: I, you and he committed a blunder.
options.B: You, he and I committed a blunder.
options.C: He, you and I committed a blunder.
options.D: You, I and he committed a blunder.

Sentence Correction.explanation: When confessing a mistake/blame, the order is First, Second, Third (1-2-3: I, you and he).

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "Let you and I solve this problem."

options.A: Let you and me solve this problem.
options.B: Let you and myself solve this problem.
options.C: Let he and I solve this problem.
options.D: Let you and we solve this problem.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Let" is followed by objective case pronouns ("you and me").

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "No less than fifty students were present."

options.A: No fewer than fifty students were present.
options.B: No lesser than fifty students were present.
options.C: Not less than fifty students were present.
options.D: No few than fifty students were present.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Fewer" is used for countable nouns ("fifty students"), whereas "less" is for uncountable.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He is both intelligent as well as hardworking."

options.A: He is both intelligent and hardworking.
options.B: He is both intelligent also hardworking.
options.C: He is both intelligent but hardworking.
options.D: He is both intelligent with hardworking.

Sentence Correction.explanation: The correlative conjunction "both" is strictly paired with "and".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "I will not go lest you should not accompany me."

options.A: I will not go lest you should accompany me.
options.B: I will not go lest you accompany me not.
options.C: I will not go lest you will accompany me.
options.D: I will not go lest you do not accompany me.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Lest" is already negative and takes "should" without an extra "not".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "She sings good."
Sentence Correction.explanation: "Well" is the adverb modifying the verb "sings"; "good" is an adjective.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "The committee have passed the resolution unanimously."

options.A: The committee has passed the resolution unanimously.
options.B: The committee have been passed the resolution.
options.C: The committee were passed the resolution.
options.D: The committees has passed the resolution.

Sentence Correction.explanation: A collective noun acting as a single unanimous entity takes a singular verb ("has").

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He returned back from Karachi yesterday."

options.B: He returned back to Karachi yesterday.
options.C: He has returned back from Karachi.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Returned back" is a redundant tautology; "returned" suffices.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "She is too happy to see you."

options.A: She is very happy to see you.
options.B: She is much happy to see you.
options.C: She is so happy to see you.
options.D: She is enough happy to see you.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Too" has an excessively negative connotation; "very happy" is correct.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He gave me a five-rupees note."

options.A: He gave me a five-rupee note.
options.B: He gave me a five-rupee notes.
options.D: He gave me a five-rupees notes.

Sentence Correction.explanation: Hyphenated compound adjectives of quantity remain singular ("five-rupee note").

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "I congratulated him for his success."

options.A: I congratulated him on his success.
options.B: I congratulated him at his success.
options.C: I congratulated him with his success.
options.D: I congratulated him to his success.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Congratulate" takes the fixed preposition "on".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "He is confident to win the match."

options.A: He is confident of winning the match.
options.B: He is confident for winning the match.
options.C: He is confident in win the match.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Confident" is followed by "of + gerund".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct: "None of the two boys came."

options.A: Neither of the two boys came.
options.B: No one of the two boys came.
options.C: Not any of the two boys came.
options.D: Neither of the two boy came.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Neither" is used when referring to two persons; "none" is for three or more.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence:

options.A: Neither the captain nor the players were satisfied with the decision.
options.B: Neither the captain nor the players was satisfied with the decision.
options.C: Neither the captain or the players were satisfied with the decision.
options.D: Neither the captain nor the players has been satisfied with the decision.

Sentence Correction.explanation: With "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("players" -> plural verb "were").

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct the error: "He is more taller than his elder brother."

options.A: He is taller than his elder brother.
options.B: He is most taller than his elder brother.
options.C: He is more tall than his elder brother.
options.D: He is taller then his elder brother.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "More taller" is an incorrect double comparative; "taller" is sufficient.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Identify the correct sentence containing parallel structure:

options.A: She enjoys reading historical novels, playing the piano, and swimming.
options.B: She enjoys reading historical novels, to play the piano, and swimming.
options.C: She enjoys reading historical novels, piano playing, and to swim.
options.D: She enjoys to read novels, playing the piano, and swim.

Sentence Correction.explanation: All three coordinate elements must share the same grammatical form (gerunds: reading, playing, swimming).

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Choose the correct version of the sentence: "One of the boys have forgotten his notebook."

options.A: One of the boys has forgotten his notebook.
options.B: One of the boys have forgotten their notebook.
options.C: One of the boy has forgotten his notebook.
options.D: One of the boys had forgot their notebook.

Sentence Correction.explanation: The subject is "One" (singular), so it takes the singular verb "has" and singular pronoun "his".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Identify the sentence that fixes the dangling modifier: "Walking through the orchard, the apples caught my attention."

options.A: While I was walking through the orchard, the apples caught my attention.
options.B: Walking through the orchard, my attention was caught by apples.
options.C: Walking through the orchard, the apples were seen by me.
options.D: Having walked through the orchard, apples caught my eye.

Sentence Correction.explanation: The introductory participle must logically modify the agent ("I"), not "the apples".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Correct the error in: "He did not know nothing about the upcoming examination."

options.A: He did not know anything about the upcoming examination.
options.B: He did know nothing about the upcoming examination.
options.C: He did not know no thing about the upcoming examination.
options.D: He does not know nothing about the upcoming examination.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Did not know nothing" is an incorrect double negative. Use "anything" with "not".

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: Scarcely had he reached the station when the train departed.
options.B: Scarcely had he reached the station than the train departed.
options.C: Scarcely had he reached the station then the train departed.
options.D: Scarcely he had reached the station when the train departed.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Scarcely...when" is the correct correlative pair with inverted subject-auxiliary order ("had he reached").

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Select the grammatically accurate sentence:

options.A: The furniture in this showroom is made of solid oak.
options.B: The furnitures in this showroom are made of solid oak.
options.C: The furnitures in this showroom is made of solid oak.
options.D: The furniture in this showroom are made of solid oak.

Sentence Correction.explanation: "Furniture" is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb and has no plural form with -s.

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Choose the correct sentence regarding pronoun case:

options.A: Between you and me, the new proposal seems impracticable.
options.B: Between you and I, the new proposal seems impracticable.
options.C: Between you and myself, the new proposal seems impracticable.
options.D: Between he and I, the new proposal seems impracticable.

Sentence Correction.explanation: Prepositions (like "Between") take objective case pronouns ("you and me").

Sentence Correction.subject: English
Sentence Correction.topic: Grammar mechanics, agreement, parallelism, and modifiers
Sentence Correction.question: Identify the sentence free of punctuation and agreement errors:

options.A: Ten kilometers is a considerable distance to walk on foot.
options.B: Ten kilometers are a considerable distance to walk on foot.
options.C: Ten kilometer is a considerable distance to walk on foot.
options.D: Ten kilometers are considerable distances to walk on foot.

Sentence Correction.explanation: A plural quantity of distance, time, or money regarded as a single unit takes a singular verb ("is").

Types of Sentences.subject: English

Types of Sentences.question: Identify the sentence type: "Although it rained heavily, we attended the match."
Types of Sentences.explanation: Contains one subordinate clause ("Although it rained...") and one independent clause.

Types of Sentences.question: Identify the type: "The bell rang, and the students entered the hall."

Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals

Types of Sentences.explanation: Contains a single independent clause with one finite verb.

Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "Please close the front gate."

Types of Sentences.question: A declarative sentence is primarily used to:

Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals

Types of Sentences.explanation: Contains a single subject and a single finite verb with a participial adjective.

Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "Would that I were a bird!"
Types of Sentences.explanation: "Would that" expresses a strong unrealizable wish/supplication.

Types of Sentences.subject: English
Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "He ran fast yet he missed the bus."
Types of Sentences.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by coordinating conjunction "yet".

Types of Sentences.explanation: Contains a defining relative clause ("who stole the necklace").

Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "God save the Queen!"
Types of Sentences.explanation: Expresses a prayer/wish in the traditional subjunctive optative mood.

Types of Sentences.explanation: An imperative sentence issuing a moral prohibition.

Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "Is she preparing for the examination?"
Types of Sentences.explanation: An interrogative sentence beginning with an auxiliary verb seeking yes/no.

Types of Sentences.subject: English

Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "The sun having risen, the fog dispersed."
Types of Sentences.explanation: Uses a participial phrase in nominative absolute construction with one main clause.

Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "He finished his work and went home, but his friend stayed back."
Types of Sentences.explanation: Three independent clauses coordinated by "and" and "but".

Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "Since you insist, I shall accompany you."

Types of Sentences.subject: English
Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "Listen to what your parents say."
Types of Sentences.explanation: An imperative main clause taking a noun clause as prepositional object.

Types of Sentences.subject: English
Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Identify: "Hurrah! Pakistan won the cricket championship!"

Types of Sentences.explanation: An inverted Shakespearean imperative sentence offering moral counsel.

Types of Sentences.explanation: Traditional patriotic optative blessing.

Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Which sentence structure allows maximum density of information?

Types of Sentences.subject: English

Types of Sentences.question: Identify the compound sentence:

Types of Sentences.subject: English

Types of Sentences.question: Identify the Third Conditional sentence:

Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: What is the function of the sentence: "May you achieve brilliant success in your future endeavors!"?

Types of Sentences.question: Identify the structural classification of: "The children played happily in the newly opened park until dusk."

Types of Sentences.subject: English
Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Which sentence is a Compound-Complex sentence?

Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Identify the Second Conditional sentence:

options.A: If I were the head of the committee, I would introduce transparent policies.
options.B: If I am the head of the committee, I will introduce transparent policies.
options.C: If I had been the head of the committee, I would have introduced transparent policies.
options.D: If water freezes, it turns into solid ice.

Types of Sentences.explanation: Second conditional (hypothetical present/future): If + subjunctive were / past simple, would + base verb.

Types of Sentences.subject: English
Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: What type of sentence is: "How magnificent the Himalayan peaks look at sunrise!"?
Types of Sentences.explanation: It expresses strong emotion and wonder, ending with an exclamation mark.

Types of Sentences.subject: English
Types of Sentences.topic: Simple, Compound, Complex, Declarative, Interrogative, Conditionals
Types of Sentences.question: Identify the sentence containing an adverbial condition clause (Zero Conditional):

options.A: If water reaches 100 degrees Celsius, it boils.
options.B: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
options.C: If you had arrived on time, we would have met him.
options.D: If I possessed wings, I would fly across oceans.

Types of Sentences.explanation: Zero conditional expresses universal cause-and-effect: If + Simple Present, Simple Present.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Bread and butter ______ his favorite breakfast."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: When two nouns express a single compound idea or dish, singular verb "is" is used.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Either the teacher or the students ______ responsible."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: With "either...or", the verb agrees with the nearer plural subject ("students").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The quality of these mangoes ______ not good."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: The subject is singular "quality", not plural "mangoes".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Neither of the candidates ______ qualified."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Distributive pronoun "Neither" takes a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The jury ______ divided in their opinions."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: When members of a collective noun act individually or disagree, plural verb "were" is used.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Physics ______ an interesting branch of science."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Subject names ending in -s are grammatically singular.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The news ______ true."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "News" is uncountable and singular.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The captain along with his team members ______ arriving today."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Parenthetical phrases like "along with" do not affect the main singular subject "captain".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Fifty thousand rupees ______ a large amount."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: A sum of money regarded as a singular whole takes a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Many a student ______ failed in the test."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "Many a + singular noun" is followed by a singular verb ("has").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "A number of students ______ waiting outside."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "A number of" takes a plural verb, whereas "The number of" takes singular.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The number of applicants ______ fifty."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "The number of" takes a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Every boy and every girl ______ given a prize."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Nouns qualified by "every" connected by "and" require a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "No news ______ good news."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "News" governs singular verb "is".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Gulliver's Travels ______ written by Jonathan Swift."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Titles of single books take a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Neither you nor I ______ to blame."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: With "neither...nor", verb agrees in person with the closer subject ("I am").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Two-thirds of the city ______ destroyed by fire."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Fractions of an uncountable/singular noun ("city") take a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Two-thirds of the books ______ sold."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Fractions of a plural countable noun ("books") take a plural verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The Arabian Nights ______ still a popular book."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Title of a literary collection takes a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Time and tide ______ for no man."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Traditional plural agreement for "Time and tide".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "More than one person ______ involved in the fraud."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "More than one + singular noun" takes a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Slow and steady ______ the race."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Compound singular subject expressing a single concept takes singular verb "wins".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The Prime Minister as well as his cabinet ministers ______ present."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "As well as" does not alter the singular subject "Prime Minister".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The cattle ______ grazing in the meadow."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "Cattle" is inherently plural.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The scissors ______ very sharp."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Two-part instruments (scissors, tongs, spectacles) take plural verbs.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "A pair of scissors ______ kept on the desk."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "A pair of" is singular and takes a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Measles ______ an infectious disease."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Disease names ending in -s (measles, mumps) take singular verbs.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Not only Ali but also his brothers ______ invited."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Verb agrees with the closer subject "brothers" (plural).

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Everybody ______ done his duty."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Indefinite pronoun "Everybody" takes singular verb "has".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "All that glitters ______ not gold."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Standard proverb uses singular verb "is".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Ten kilometers ______ not a long walk for an athlete."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Distance as a single measure takes a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The United States ______ a powerful nation."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Country names take singular verbs.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "One of my friends ______ living in Canada."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Singular subject "One" governs "is".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "None of the money ______ recovered."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "Money" is uncountable, so "none" takes singular verb "was".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Politics ______ a complicated field."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "Politics" takes a singular verb when referring to the field/discipline.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The police ______ investigating the case."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "Police" is a collective plural noun.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "The majority of students ______ passed."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "Majority of + plural noun" takes a plural verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "A bouquet of yellow roses ______ presented to the guest."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Subject is singular "bouquet".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "There ______ many reasons for his absence."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: With dummy "There", verb agrees with following plural subject "many reasons".

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: "Neither of the two roads ______ to the railway station."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "Neither" takes a singular verb ("leads").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Choose the correct verb: "The jury ________ divided in their individual opinions."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: When members of a collective noun act individually or have differing opinions ("their opinions"), a plural verb ("were") is used.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Select the correct sentence:

options.A: Bread and butter is a staple breakfast in many households.
options.B: Bread and butter are a staple breakfast in many households.
options.C: Bread and butter were a staple breakfast in many households.
options.D: Bread and butter have been a staple breakfast in many households.

Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: When two nouns express a single compound idea or unit (bread and butter as a dish), the verb is singular ("is").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Choose the correct verb: "The commander, along with his brave soldiers, ________ awarded medals."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Intervening parenthetical phrases introduced by "along with" do not change the number of the subject ("commander" is singular -> "was").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Fill in the blank: "Every one of the participants ________ given a participation certificate."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "Every one" is an indefinite singular pronoun requiring a singular verb ("was").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Select the grammatically correct option: "Neither the teacher nor the students ________ present in the auditorium."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: With "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("students" is plural -> "were").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Choose the correct verb: "A number of qualified candidates ________ applied for the internship."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "A number of" takes a plural verb ("have applied"), whereas "The number of" takes a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Fill in the blank: "The news broadcast by the national media ________ verified by official sources."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "News" is singular in construction and takes a singular verb ("was").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Select the correct form: "Mathematics ________ considered a compulsory subject in secondary school."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: Names of subjects/disciplines ending in -s (Mathematics, Physics, Civics) take a singular verb.

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Fill in the blank: "Fifty thousand rupees ________ a reasonable sum for this repair work."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: A specific amount of money thought of as a single total quantity takes a singular verb ("is").

Subject-Verb Agreement.subject: English
Subject-Verb Agreement.topic: Rules of proximity, collective nouns, compound subjects
Subject-Verb Agreement.question: Choose the correct verb: "More than one candidate ________ selected for the scholarship."
Subject-Verb Agreement.explanation: "More than one" is followed by a singular noun and takes a singular verb ("was").

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He is very fond ______ classical music."
Prepositions.explanation: The adjective "fond" takes the fixed preposition "of".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "The train arrived ______ the station on time."
Prepositions.explanation: "Arrive at" is used for specific buildings or small points.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "Distribute these sweets ______ the two sisters."
Prepositions.explanation: "Between" is used for two entities; "among" is for three or more.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He was accused ______ murder."
Prepositions.explanation: "Accused" takes the fixed preposition "of".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "She was born ______ 14th August 1947."
Prepositions.explanation: "On" is used before specific calendar dates.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "The cat jumped ______ the table."
Prepositions.explanation: "Onto" signifies movement toward a surface.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He has been absent ______ Monday."
Prepositions.explanation: "Since" indicates a specific starting point in time.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He is addicted ______ gambling."
Prepositions.explanation: "Addicted" takes "to".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "The frog jumped ______ the pond."
Prepositions.explanation: "Into" expresses movement from outside to inside a container/liquid.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He is good ______ mathematics."
Prepositions.explanation: Proficiency in a skill or subject uses "good at".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "She is senior ______ me by two years."
Prepositions.explanation: Comparative adjectives ending in -ior take "to".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "The meeting will start ______ 9:00 AM."
Prepositions.explanation: "At" is used for exact points of clock time.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "We traveled to Murree ______ bus."
Prepositions.explanation: Modes of public transport without article use "by" ("by bus").

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He prevented me ______ entering the lab."
Prepositions.explanation: "Prevent" takes "from + gerund".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "You must abide ______ the school rules."
Prepositions.explanation: "Abide by" means to conform to or follow rules.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He died ______ cholera."
Prepositions.explanation: Death directly caused by a disease takes "of".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "She is proud ______ her achievements."
Prepositions.explanation: "Proud" takes "of".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "I prefer tea ______ coffee."
Prepositions.explanation: "Prefer" is followed by "to".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He is envious ______ his neighbor's new car."
Prepositions.explanation: "Envious" takes "of".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He is blind ______ his own shortcomings."
Prepositions.explanation: Metaphorical blindness to defects takes "blind to".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "The river flows ______ the old stone bridge."
Prepositions.explanation: "Under" is standard for movement directly below a structure.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He congratulated me ______ passing the examination."
Prepositions.explanation: "Congratulate" takes "on".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He is eligible ______ the scholarship."
Prepositions.explanation: "Eligible" takes "for".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "She is married ______ a renowned surgeon."
Prepositions.explanation: Passive/adjectival "married" takes "to".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He has no passion ______ politics."
Prepositions.explanation: "Passion" takes "for".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "We must beware ______ pickpockets."
Prepositions.explanation: "Beware" takes "of".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He was guilty ______ negligence."
Prepositions.explanation: "Guilty" takes "of".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "I agree ______ you on this matter."
Prepositions.explanation: Agreeing with a person takes "agree with".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He agreed ______ my proposal."
Prepositions.explanation: Agreeing to a plan/proposal takes "agree to".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He is confident ______ victory."
Prepositions.explanation: "Confident" takes "of".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "The airplane flew ______ the clouds."
Prepositions.explanation: "Above" indicates higher level/elevation.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He jumped ______ the wall to escape."
Prepositions.explanation: "Over" denotes movement across and above a barrier.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "She excels ______ mathematics and physics."
Prepositions.explanation: "Excel" takes "in".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "The dog is faithful ______ its master."
Prepositions.explanation: "Faithful" takes "to".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "Smoking is injurious ______ health."
Prepositions.explanation: "Injurious" takes "to".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He was astonished ______ the unexpected results."
Prepositions.explanation: "Astonished" takes "at".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "He apologized ______ his rude behavior."
Prepositions.explanation: Apologizing for an action uses "apologize for".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "She insisted ______ paying the bill herself."
Prepositions.explanation: "Insist" takes "on + gerund".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "They were surprised ______ the sudden announcement."
Prepositions.explanation: "Surprised" takes "at" for non-agent events.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: "The sun sets ______ the west."
Prepositions.explanation: "In" is used for cardinal compass directions.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: "The judge acquitted the accused ________ all charges."
Prepositions.explanation: The standard dependent preposition with "acquit" is "of" (acquit someone of a charge).

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Fill in the blank: "She is thoroughly proficient ________ three foreign languages."
Prepositions.explanation: "Proficient" is followed by the preposition "in" when referring to subjects or languages.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Choose the correct preposition: "The rescue boat sailed ________ the roaring waves."
Prepositions.explanation: "Through" indicates movement in a three-dimensional space or medium like waves.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Select the right preposition: "You must comply ________ the laboratory safety regulations."
Prepositions.explanation: "Comply" takes the preposition "with" (comply with rules/regulations).

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Fill in the blank: "He prevented his younger brother ________ entering the restricted area."
Prepositions.explanation: "Prevent" takes the preposition "from" followed by a gerund (prevent someone from doing something).

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Choose the correct preposition: "The final semester results will be announced ________ Monday morning."
Prepositions.explanation: Specific days and dates take the preposition "on" ("on Monday morning").

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Fill in the blank: "The athlete was disqualified for not adhering ________ the competition code."
Prepositions.explanation: "Adhere" takes the fixed preposition "to" (adhere to rules/standards).

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Choose the right preposition: "The inheritance was divided equally ________ the three siblings."
Prepositions.explanation: "Among" is used when distributing or dividing between three or more entities.

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Select the correct preposition: "He is senior ________ me in both academic rank and experience."
Prepositions.explanation: Latin comparatives ending in -ior (senior, junior, superior, inferior) take "to", never "than".

Prepositions.subject: English
Prepositions.topic: Prepositions of time, place, direction, and dependent prepositions
Prepositions.question: Fill in the blank: "The old banyan tree stands ________ the edge of the river bank."
Prepositions.explanation: "At the edge" is the standard prepositional phrase indicating a precise point.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He worked hard ______ he failed in the test."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Yet" shows contrast between hard work and failure.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Run fast ______ you will miss the train."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Work carefully lest you ______ stumble."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Neither Ali ______ Asad came to the meeting."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Either you leave ______ I will call security."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "She is not only intelligent ______ also very kind."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Both Ahmad ______ Bilal were selected."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He could not attend ______ he was severely ill."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Because" introduces the adverb clause of reason.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Although he is wealthy, ______ he is humble."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Although" may be paired with "yet" or a comma, never "but".

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Wait here ______ I come back."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Until" expresses time up to a specific event.

Conjunctions.question: "You will not pass ______ you work hard."

Conjunctions.question: "No sooner had he left ______ it began to rain."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Hardly had the teacher entered ______ the students stood up."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Scarcely had we reached the station ______ the train departed."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "I do not know ______ he will come or not."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Whether" is used when followed by an explicit "or not".

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He was tired, ______ he went to bed early."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He missed the bus ______ he woke up late."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Make hay ______ the sun shines."
Conjunctions.explanation: "While" expresses action during a period of time.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "As you sow, ______ shall you reap."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He is as wise ______ he is brave."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He behaves as if he ______ the owner."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Though he is poor, ______ he is honest."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Though" is paired with "yet" or a comma.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "We eat ______ we may live."
Conjunctions.explanation: "that / so that" introduces a clause of purpose.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He was so tired ______ he could not walk."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "FANBOYS is a mnemonic for which conjunctions?"
Conjunctions.explanation: FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He will not come ______ it rains."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He worked hard so that he ______ secure first position."
Conjunctions.explanation: Past purpose clause takes "so that + might".

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "She is richer ______ her neighbor."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He walked fast ______ he should be late."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Is this question difficult ______ easy?"

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "I like him ______ he is sincere."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He neither smiled ______ spoke."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Not only the students ______ the teacher was present."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Five years have passed ______ I saw him."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Since" joins present perfect main clause with past simple time clause.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He will succeed ______ he works diligently."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He was guilty, ______ he was punished."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "I shall not go ______ you come with me."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "The sun set ______ the stars appeared."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "He is old ______ he is energetic."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: "Such men ______ are truthful command respect."

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: "Make haste, ________ you will miss the morning departure."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Or" / "otherwise" expresses an alternative consequence or warning after an imperative.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Fill in the blank: "Walk cautiously ________ you should stumble on the rocky path."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Lest" expresses negative purpose and is followed by the modal "should".

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Select the correct correlative conjunction: "No sooner had the bell rung ________ the students rushed out."
Conjunctions.explanation: "No sooner" is strictly correlated with "than" ("No sooner... than").

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: "We cannot grant approval ________ you produce the official NOC."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Unless" introduces a negative condition meaning "if not" or "except on condition that".

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Identify the subordinating conjunction expressing reason/cause:

options.A: Since it was raining heavily, the outdoor parade was called off.
options.B: He ran fast, but he could not catch the bus.
options.C: You may go either today or tomorrow.
options.D: Neither the boy nor his sister was present.

Conjunctions.explanation: "Since" functions here as a subordinating conjunction of cause/reason.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Fill in the blank: "He was not only a gifted orator ________ a compassionate leader."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Not only" pairs strictly with the correlative conjunction "but also".

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: "Wait here ________ the traffic lights turn green."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Until" indicates time up to a specific event or point.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Identify the coordinating conjunction expressing contrast:
Conjunctions.explanation: In FANBOYS, "yet" and "but" express concession and contrast between clauses.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Select the correct conjunction: "________ he worked tirelessly day and night, his business faced losses."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Although" introduces a subordinate clause of concession/contrast.

Conjunctions.subject: English
Conjunctions.question: Fill in the blank: "He spoke with such confidence ________ everyone believed his story."
Conjunctions.explanation: "Such... that" is a correlative construction showing cause and resulting effect.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He is ______ honest police officer."
Articles.explanation: "Honest" begins with a silent 'h' and a vowel sound /ɒ/, requiring "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "She is studying at ______ university in Lahore."
Articles.explanation: "University" begins with a consonant glide sound /j/, requiring "a".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ Indus is the longest river in Pakistan."
Articles.explanation: Names of rivers take the definite article "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He is ______ best student in the class."
Articles.explanation: Superlative adjectives ("best") take "the".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ gold is a precious metal."
Articles.explanation: Material nouns in a general sense take no article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ gold in this ring is 24-carat pure."
Articles.explanation: Specific, identified material takes the definite article "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He bought ______ European car."
Articles.explanation: "European" begins with the consonant sound /j/, taking "a".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "She plays ______ violin beautifully."
Articles.explanation: Musical instruments take "the" when referring to playing them.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ sun rises in the east."
Articles.explanation: Unique celestial bodies take "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He is ______ M.A. in English Literature."
Articles.explanation: "M.A." is pronounced with an initial vowel sound /ɛm/, taking "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He is ______ one-eyed man."
Articles.explanation: "One" begins with the consonant sound /w/, taking "a".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ higher you go, the cooler it is."
Articles.explanation: Double comparatives take "The...the...".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ Holy Quran is the final divine book."
Articles.explanation: Sacred holy scriptures take "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "Mount Everest is ______ highest peak in the world."
Articles.explanation: Individual mountain peaks take no article, but superlative "highest" takes "the".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He goes to school by ______ bus."
Articles.explanation: Prepositional phrases of transport ("by bus", "by car") take zero article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ rich should help the poor."
Articles.explanation: "The + adjective" represents a whole class/plural group.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "What ______ lovely weather!"
Articles.explanation: "Weather" is uncountable and takes no indefinite article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "What ______ brilliant idea!"
Articles.explanation: Countable singular exclamation takes "What a...".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He returned home after ______ hour."
Articles.explanation: "Hour" has a silent 'h' and vowel sound, taking "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ breakfast is ready on the dining table."
Articles.explanation: Names of regular meals take zero article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ breakfast we had at the resort was lavish."
Articles.explanation: A specific, particularized meal takes "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He is ______ honorable gentleman."
Articles.explanation: "Honorable" begins with a vowel sound, taking "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ English is an international language."
Articles.explanation: Names of languages take zero article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ English defeated the French at Waterloo."
Articles.explanation: "The English" refers to the English people/nation.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He is ______ heir to a vast ancestral estate."
Articles.explanation: "Heir" begins with a silent 'h' (/ɛər/), taking "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ Himalayas lie to the north of Pakistan."
Articles.explanation: Mountain ranges take the definite article "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He went to ______ hospital to visit his sick friend."
Articles.explanation: Visiting hospital for non-treatment purpose takes "the".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He was admitted to ______ hospital for surgery."
Articles.explanation: Using an institution for its primary purpose takes zero article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ man is mortal."
Articles.explanation: "Man" in the generic sense of humanity takes no article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "She has ______ unique style of writing."
Articles.explanation: "Unique" starts with the consonant sound /j/, taking "a".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He is ______ SDO in the Irrigation Department."
Articles.explanation: "SDO" begins with vowel sound /ɛs/, taking "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth."
Articles.explanation: Oceans take "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ knowledge is power."
Articles.explanation: Abstract nouns in general sense take no article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ knowledge of physics he displayed was impressive."
Articles.explanation: Specific, defined knowledge takes "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He is ______ honest man."
Articles.explanation: "Honest" takes "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He bought ______ umbrella yesterday."
Articles.explanation: "Umbrella" begins with a short vowel sound /ʌ/, taking "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ Taj Mahal is located in Agra."
Articles.explanation: Historical monuments take "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "She wants to become ______ engineer."
Articles.explanation: "Engineer" begins with vowel sound, taking "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "______ United Kingdom consists of four countries."
Articles.explanation: Countries with words like "United", "Kingdom", "Republic" take "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: "He was elected ______ President of the society."
Articles.explanation: Titles denoting unique posts following verbs like "elected", "appointed" take zero article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Choose the correct article: "He is ________ heir to a vast ancestral estate."
Articles.explanation: "Heir" begins with a silent 'h' and a vowel sound (/ɛər/), requiring the indefinite article "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Select the correct sentence regarding article usage with superlatives:

options.A: Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world.
options.B: Mount Everest is a highest mountain peak in the world.
options.C: Mount Everest is highest mountain peak in the world.
options.D: The Mount Everest is the highest peak in world.

Articles.explanation: Superlative adjectives ("highest") take the definite article "the", while individual mountain peaks do not take "the".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Fill in the blank: "The Indus is ________ longest river in Pakistan."
Articles.explanation: Names of rivers take "the" (The Indus) and superlatives take "the" ("the longest").

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Choose the correct option: "________ gold mined in South Africa is of superior quality."
Articles.explanation: When a material noun is made particular by a qualifying clause ("mined in South Africa"), it takes "The".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Fill in the blank: "She aspires to study at ________ European university next year."
Articles.explanation: "European" begins with the consonant glide sound /j/ (yoo-ro-pe-an), so it takes "a", not "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Choose the correct article for the musical instrument: "He has been practicing on ________ violin since childhood."
Articles.explanation: Musical instruments take the definite article "the" when referring to playing or practicing them.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Select the sentence with zero article (omission of article):

options.B: The honesty is the best policy.
options.C: An honesty is the best policy.

Articles.explanation: Abstract nouns used in a general sense ("Honesty") take no article.

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Fill in the blank: "________ higher you climb, ________ colder it gets."
Articles.explanation: Parallel double comparative structures take "The + comparative, the + comparative".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Choose the correct article: "He returned home after ________ hour of rigorous training."
Articles.explanation: "Hour" begins with a silent 'h' and a vowel sound (/aʊər/), requiring "an".

Articles.subject: English
Articles.topic: Indefinite, Definite, and Zero articles usage
Articles.question: Fill in the blank: "________ Holy Quran is the sacred scripture of Islam."
Articles.explanation: Holy scriptures and sacred religious books take the definite article "The".

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which punctuation mark is used to separate items in a series of three or more?
Punctuation.explanation: Commas are used to separate series of words, phrases, or clauses.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Select the correctly punctuated direct speech interrogative sentence:
Punctuation.explanation: Question marks inside speech quotes belong within the quotation marks.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which mark is used to introduce a formal list or long quotation?
Punctuation.explanation: A colon is used to introduce formal lists, enumerations, or direct quotes.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which mark connects two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction?
Punctuation.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses without coordinating conjunctions.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Identify the sentence with the correct use of the apostrophe:

options.A: The children's toys were scattered on the floor.
options.B: The childrens' toys were scattered on the floor.

Punctuation.explanation: Irregular plural nouns not ending in -s form possession with "'s" (children's).

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Distinguish between "its" and "it's":

options.A: "Its" is possessive; "it's" is the contraction of "it is" or "it has".
options.C: Both are interchangeable in formal English.
options.D: "Its" is a verb; "it's" is a noun.

Punctuation.explanation: "Its" indicates possession without apostrophe; "it's" is a contraction.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which sentence correctly uses hyphens in a compound adjective?

options.B: He is a well known scientist.

Punctuation.explanation: Compound modifiers preceding a noun are hyphenated ("well-known scientist").

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: What is the correct punctuation for direct address?

options.A: Yes, Sir, I have understood the concept.
options.B: Yes Sir I have understood the concept.
options.C: Yes, Sir I have understood, the concept.
options.D: Yes Sir, I have, understood the concept.

Punctuation.explanation: Direct address terms are set off by commas on both sides.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Select the correctly punctuated sentence containing a noun in apposition:

options.A: Lahore, the capital of Punjab, is famous for historical gardens.
options.B: Lahore the capital of Punjab is famous for historical gardens.
options.C: Lahore, the capital of Punjab is famous, for historical gardens.
options.D: Lahore the capital, of Punjab, is famous.

Punctuation.explanation: Nouns in apposition ("the capital of Punjab") must be enclosed by commas.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which mark is used to indicate an omission of letters or numbers?
Punctuation.explanation: An apostrophe denotes missing letters in contractions (don't, '99).

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which mark indicates an abrupt pause or sudden change of thought?
Punctuation.explanation: An em-dash signals a dramatic parenthetical pause or shift in tone.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which mark is used to indicate words omitted from a quoted text?
Punctuation.explanation: Three consecutive dots (ellipsis) signify omitted quoted material.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Choose the correctly capitalized and punctuated sentence:

options.A: Dr. Ahmad visited the Quaid-e-Azam Academy on Friday.
options.B: dr. ahmad visited the quaid-e-azam academy on friday.
options.C: Dr Ahmad visited the quaid-e-Azam Academy on Friday.
options.D: Dr. Ahmad visited the Quaid-E-Azam academy on friday.

Punctuation.explanation: Proper titles, names, institutions, and days of the week require capital letters.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Where should the comma be placed in a introductory adverbial clause?

options.C: At the very end of the sentence
options.D: Between the subject and its verb

Punctuation.explanation: Introductory dependent clauses are separated from the main clause by a comma.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Correct punctuation for contractions:

options.A: They aren't coming to the seminar.
options.B: They arent' coming to the seminar.
options.C: They are'nt coming to the seminar.
options.D: They aren't coming, to the seminar.

Punctuation.explanation: The apostrophe replaces the missing letter "o" in "are not" -> "aren't".

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Select the correct plural possessive:

options.A: The boys' hostel is located near the stadium.
options.B: The boy's hostel is located near the stadium (referring to multiple boys).
options.C: The boyses' hostel is located near the stadium.
options.D: The boys hostel' is located near the stadium.

Punctuation.explanation: Regular plural nouns ending in -s form possession with a trailing apostrophe only (boys').

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which sentence correctly encloses a non-defining relative clause?

options.A: My elder brother, who is an engineer, lives in Quetta.
options.B: My elder brother who is an engineer, lives in Quetta.
options.C: My elder brother who is an engineer lives in Quetta.
options.D: My elder brother, who is an engineer lives in Quetta.

Punctuation.explanation: Non-restrictive relative clauses are non-essential and enclosed by commas.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Identify the sentence with correct quotation marks:

options.A: "To be or not to be," said Hamlet, "that is the question."
options.B: "To be or not to be" said Hamlet "that is the question."
options.C: "To be or not to be", said Hamlet, "that is the question".
options.D: To be or not to be said Hamlet that is the question.

Punctuation.explanation: Divided quotes place commas and attribution tags properly outside speech text.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Select the sentence demonstrating correct use of semicolons in a complex list:

options.A: We visited Paris, France; Rome, Italy; and Madrid, Spain.
options.B: We visited Paris, France, Rome, Italy, and Madrid, Spain.
options.C: We visited Paris; France, Rome; Italy, and Madrid; Spain.
options.D: We visited Paris: France; Rome: Italy; and Madrid: Spain.

Punctuation.explanation: Semicolons separate list items that already contain internal commas.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which terminal mark belongs at the end of: "How incredible this victory is"
Punctuation.explanation: Exclamatory sentences end with an exclamation mark.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Identify the sentence with correct parenthetical punctuation:

options.A: The novel (published in 1925) became an instant literary masterpiece.
options.B: The novel, (published in 1925), became an instant masterpiece.
options.C: The novel (published in 1925 became an instant masterpiece).
options.D: The novel published in 1925) became an instant masterpiece.

Punctuation.explanation: Parentheses enclose supplementary information cleanly without external duplicate commas.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Select the correctly capitalized book title:

options.A: The Old Man and the Sea
options.B: The Old man And The Sea
options.C: The old Man and The sea
options.D: the Old Man and the Sea

Punctuation.explanation: Major words are capitalized; articles, prepositions, and conjunctions remain lowercase unless first.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which punctuation mark joins prefixes to root words (e.g., "co-worker")?
Punctuation.explanation: Hyphens join prefixes to words or link compound word elements.

Punctuation.question: Correct punctuation for time indication:
Punctuation.explanation: A colon separates hours and minutes in time notation.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which mark is used at the end of an indirect question: "He asked where I lived"
Punctuation.explanation: Indirect questions are declarative in form and conclude with a full stop.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: Which sentence correctly punctuates transitional conjunctive adverbs?

options.A: He worked hard; however, he did not win the prize.
options.B: He worked hard, however, he did not win the prize.
options.C: He worked hard however; he did not win the prize.
options.D: He worked hard; however he did not win the prize,

Punctuation.explanation: Conjunctive adverbs joining clauses take a preceding semicolon and following comma.

Punctuation.subject: English
Punctuation.question: What is the error in: "Its raining outside."?
Punctuation.explanation: "It's" (it is) requires an apostrophe.

Punctuation.question: Select the correctly punctuated address salutation in a formal letter:
Punctuation.explanation: Salutations in British/Pakistani formal correspondence take a comma.
